target.title: fix(plugins): resolve public artifacts from installed plugin roots
target.body:
Fixes #98740

## What Problem This Solves

After the 2026.6.11 Mattermost plugin externalization, every native `/oc_*` slash command callback is rejected with `401` by the gateway before the plugin's handler runs. `/api/channels/*` is a protected plugin-route prefix (`src/gateway/security-path.ts`), and the only exemption — the channel's `gateway-auth-api.js` public artifact — was resolved by a **bundled-only** loader (`src/plugins/public-surface-loader.ts` → `src/plugins/public-surface-runtime.ts`). `openclaw@2026.6.11` no longer ships `dist/extensions/mattermost/**` (externalized, `bundledDist: false`), and the resolver never consulted installed plugin roots under `~/.openclaw/npm/...`, so the bypass set resolved empty and gateway bearer auth was enforced against Mattermost's callbacks. Registration (outbound) and DMs/@mentions (WebSocket) were unaffected, which matched the reporter's symptoms exactly.

The same bundled-only resolution silently degraded every other plugin public artifact for externalized installs: doctor contract (`doctor-contract-api.js`), secret contract (`channel-contract-api`), message-tool discovery, thread-binding, media inbound roots, and bundled health checks all load through the same helper.

## Why This Change Was Made

`loadBundledPluginPublicArtifactModuleSync` now falls back to the plugin's installed package root (via `loadInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecordsSync`, the same cached install-record source install/loader flows already use) when bundled resolution misses. Candidates: `<installRoot>/dist/<artifact>` (published packages), then top-level source-extension variants (path installs). Bundled/source locations keep precedence, so source checkouts and bundled plugins behave exactly as before. The external `@openclaw/mattermost` package already ships `dist/gateway-auth-api.js` — core just never looked there.

This fixes the whole artifact class at one boundary instead of special-casing gateway auth, per the plugins-boundary rule: "Do not create private backdoors that bundled plugins can use but external plugins cannot."

Trust note: installed plugins already execute in-process with full plugin API access, so loading their public artifacts adds no new trust surface; artifact loading still goes through the same `openRootFileSync` boundary validation, with the install root as the boundary.

## User Impact

Mattermost native slash commands work again on packaged installs ≥2026.6.11 with the externalized `@openclaw/mattermost` plugin. Externalized plugins' doctor/secret/message-tool/thread-binding/inbound-root/health artifacts resolve again. No behavior change for source checkouts or bundled plugins.

## Evidence

**Unit/regression tests** — `src/plugins/public-surface-loader.test.ts` (10/10 passing): installed-root fallback resolves the artifact from a managed npm project fixture (`state/npm/projects/<proj>/node_modules/@openclaw/<pkg>/dist/...`); bundled artifacts keep precedence over installed; artifacts missing everywhere still throw the optional-artifact sentinel consumers rely on. `gateway-auth-bypass.test.ts`, `public-surface-runtime.test.ts`, `installed-plugin-index-record-reader` suites green.

**Shipped-artifact proof** — `openclaw@2026.6.10` npm tarball ships `dist/extensions/mattermost/gateway-auth-api.js`; the `openclaw@2026.6.11` tarball ships zero `dist/extensions/mattermost` files, while `@openclaw/mattermost@2026.6.11` ships `dist/gateway-auth-api.js`.

**Packaged repro matrix** — each row: real npm install, isolated state dir, gateway token auth, mattermost channel configured, external plugin installed via `openclaw plugins install @openclaw/mattermost` (lands in `state/npm/projects/openclaw-mattermost-<hash>/...`, same layout as the issue). Probe simulates the Mattermost callback (no gateway bearer, form-encoded body):

```
POST /api/channels/mattermost/command   (no gateway token, as Mattermost sends)

openclaw@2026.6.10 (bundled mattermost):
  HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
  {"response_type":"ephemeral","text":"Slash commands are not yet initialized. Please try again in a moment."}
  → reaches the plugin route (monitor idle against a dummy MM URL; auth bypass worked)

openclaw@2026.6.11 (externalized @openclaw/mattermost):
  HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
  {"error":{"message":"Unauthorized","type":"unauthorized"}}
  → gateway auth layer; the plugin is never reached (the bug)

openclaw@2026.6.11, same probe WITH the gateway bearer token:
  HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
  {"response_type":"ephemeral","text":"Slash commands are not yet initialized. Please try again in a moment."}
  → plugin route alive and reachable; ONLY gateway auth blocks Mattermost

this branch (source dist, OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1 + external plugin install = packaged topology):
  HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
  {"response_type":"ephemeral","text":"Slash commands are not yet initialized. Please try again in a moment."}
  → bypass resolved from the installed plugin root; callback passes gateway auth again
```

`git diff v2026.6.11..main` is empty for the loader/gateway files involved, so the 2026.6.11 row doubles as the without-fix control for this branch's topology.

**Pending before undraft**
- [ ] Live Mattermost round-trip (registered command token → 200 `Processing...`) against a real MM server
- [ ] `pnpm check:changed` / tsgo lanes
- [ ] Fresh autoreview pass
